name: Delvek Mate-Guava Rush
description: A caffeinated soda built on real mate extract cut with synth-guava, positioned as a cleaner, less aggressive alternative to pure energy drinks. Delvek markets it to working professionals who want sustained alertness without the crash profile of synthetic stimulant beverages.
flavor_profile: Bitter mate earthiness, bright guava sweetness, grassy undertone, medium carbonation with a clean caffeine finish
cultural_context: Delvek Mate-Guava Rush is the drink of the long shift — consumed by logistics workers, transit operators, and junior corp employees who need to stay functional without resorting to pharmaceutical stimulants. It occupies an interesting middle space: too healthy-adjacent for the energy drink crowd, too caffeinated for the casual soda market. It has genuine utility and genuine loyalty.
story_hooks: A transit authority is quietly contracting with Delvek to supply subsidized cans to night-shift operators — a union rep suspects the contract involves more than just caffeine, possibly attention-management additives.
Someone is counterfeiting Delvek cans with a significantly higher stimulant load — several workers have experienced adverse reactions, and the company is desperately trying to contain the story.

A Tier 3 nutritionist has been tracking Delvek consumption patterns in her clinic and believes the 'real mate extract' claim is partially false — but proving it means going up against Delvek Nutrition Systems' legal team.
